first.rationale: Current situation shows a competitor pressing on price-sensitive SMB segment while activation and onboarding completion are both declining. Memory 73 demonstrates that targeted promotional pricing drove strong acquisition and revenue lift while also reducing time-to-first-value for price-sensitive SMBs. Memory 31 shows onboarding simplification works, but that path alone won't address the competitive pricing pressure or activation drop simultaneously. Promotional pricing directly counters the competitor's entry move, recovers addressable SMB revenue at risk, and memory 73 indicates it improves activation speed as a secondary benefit. Verifying memory 73 (the core promotional pricing evidence) and memory 31 (to confirm onboarding baseline) will validate whether promotional pricing can be deployed with confidence this week. The scale is standard_experiment because we need real-world revenue impact data against active competition, but the precedent is strong enough to justify moving beyond guarded test. This preserves uncertainty because we're testing in a narrow but measurable segment with known competitive pressure, not broad-rolling an untested approach.
